summary.title: Shape Up: Stop Running in Circles and Ship Work that Matters
summary.one_liner: Basecamp's free book describes Shape Up, a product development method that shapes problems into bounded pitches, places bets on them in a betting table, and builds them in six-week cycles.
keywords: how to avoid running in circles
how to break down software projects
how to decide when to stop a project
takeaways: Shaping means defining the problem and a rough, bounded solution before work is handed to a team.
A pitch packages the problem, solution, boundaries, and risks so a decision can be made about it.
A betting table replaces the backlog: leadership places bets on pitches instead of ranking endless to-do lists.
Teams build a bet end to end with clear responsibility, shipping one piece at a time and mapping scopes.
Progress is shown visually, and teams decide when to stop and move on to the next cycle.
summary.summary: This is the table of contents for Basecamp's online book Shape Up, which the page presents as a method for escaping ineffective "best practices" and shipping meaningful projects. The book is organized in three parts: Shaping (principles, setting boundaries, finding elements, handling risks and rabbit holes, writing the pitch), Betting (bets instead of backlogs, the betting table, placing bets), and Building (handing over responsibility, getting one piece done, mapping scopes, showing progress, deciding when to stop, moving on). The listing shows only the chapter outline and meta description, so specific details of each chapter are not visible on this page.
